articles.summary: You, personally, will not have to pay the Millionaires Tax. That is almost certain. Starting in 2029, the Millionaires Tax, signed by Gov. Bob Ferguson this March, would tax Washington households at 9.9% on any income they make over $1 million. But chances are you’re safe — even if you have a million dollars squirreled away in the bank. As long as your household isn’t unlucky enough to be pulling in $1 million a year in income, you will be spared. Right now, there are fewer than 500 people in the three legislative districts that make up most of Spokane County who would qualify for the tax, according to Washington Department of Revenue data, and you most likely aren’t one of them. Yes, you could be a rare exception. You might be Clearwater Paper CEO Arsen Kitch or Providence executive Scott O'Brien or Gonzaga Basketball Coach Mark Few. (Mark, if you’re reading this, you would probably need to shell out at least $200,000 in taxes every year for your $3 million salary.) But Spokane is not a town of millionaires. articles.title: JD Vance Wants Politicians To Make Six Promises About Your Tax Dollars
articles.author: Drew Berkemeyer
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance launched a new six-point pledge on Thursday calling on elected officials and government leaders nationwide to join the Trump administration’s effort to root out fraud, waste, and abuse in taxpayer-funded programs, drawing support from Republican governors, members of Congress, state financial officials, and senior administration figures. “I’m calling on every member of Congress, as well as local and statewide officials, and anyone seeking public office, to rise to the occasion,” Vance said in a video announcing the pledge. The initiative builds on Vance’s role leading the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, which President Donald Trump tasked him with coordinating earlier this year. The pledge calls on signatories to protect vulnerable Americans from fraud, ensure benefits go to eligible recipients, prevent taxpayer-funded assistance dollars from being used to purchase luxury goods, coordinate across government to stop fraudulent payments before they are made, and hold convicted fraudsters accountable.
